etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Latin succedere (“to succeed in”).

definitions.definition: Coming one after the other in a series.

quote.citation: 2011 November 5, Phil Dawkes, “QPR 2 - 3 Man City”, in BBC Sport‎[1]:
quote.text: Mancini's men were far from their best but dug in to earn a 10th win in 11 league games and an eighth successive victory in all competitions to maintain their five-point lead at the top of the table.

definitions.definition: Of, or relating to a succession; hereditary.
(grammar) Of or relating to the grammatical aspect which presupposes the completion of a secondary action as a premise for the primary action of the statement.
